## The study

This study compares outcomes after kidney–pancreas and pancreas-alone transplantation between recipients with and without HIV, using the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients. It is preliminary: the analysis plan is a draft, and no results are published here.

-   **Vagish Hemmige** (study design and analysis)

Vagish Hemmige makes the scientific decisions for the project. Open decisions are listed in the project's [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/HIV-pancreas-2024-srtr/issues).

## This repository

The analysis will run as a series of scripts, sourced in order by `R/main.R`, that load the SRTR files through the [{sRtr}](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/sRtr) package. SRTR data are available only to authorized users under the SRTR data use agreement, so neither the data nor any output derived from them is stored in this repository.

Contributions follow the rules in [`AGENTS.md`](agents.qmd); known issues and open decisions are tracked in [Issues](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/HIV-pancreas-2024-srtr/issues).

## How this website was created

The site is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org) from the analysis scripts themselves. Each code page imports the labelled sections of its script from `R/` and shows them with an explanation; the site never runs the analysis, so it is built without the analysis data. A GitHub Actions workflow renders the site and publishes it whenever the main branch changes.

The repository was set up with the R Analysis Workflow plugin and an AI assistant (Claude). AI assistants work under the rules in `AGENTS.md`: they never read SRTR data, they write and test code on synthetic data only, and scientific decisions stay with the investigator.

Four documents describe the project. In short: the plan is the scientific intent, the architecture is the workflow as implemented, and `AGENTS.md` holds the rules for working together.

-   [**Analysis plan**](analysis-plan.qmd): *what the analysis is meant to do, and why.* The question, the population, the methods, and the open decisions. Code implements it and does not redefine it.
-   [**Architecture**](architecture.qmd): *how the code does it.* The scripts, the order they run in, what each needs and produces, and how data flow between them.
-   [**AGENTS.md**](agents.qmd): *how people and AI assistants work on the project.* Rules for restricted data, coding, checks, proposing changes and getting a person's approval.
-   [**Repository blueprint**](repository-blueprint.qmd): *the layout every project of this kind starts from*, which the architecture document then describes as built.

## Pages

-   [**Clinical background**](background.qmd): transplantation in people with HIV, and what is known about pancreas transplantation in particular.
-   [**Methodological background**](methodological_background.qmd): the registry data, the pancreas donor risk index, propensity-score matching and weighting, and time-to-event outcomes.
-   [**Study design and methods**](study_methods.qmd): what the study chose and why, in plain language, with the decisions still open.
-   [**Setup**](setup.qmd): packages and shared constants, including the provisional values of open decisions.
-   [**Functions**](functions.qmd): reusable helper functions, each tested on synthetic data.
